What does it take to check OpenAI's 122,458-file Lean library? Notes on mmap limits, using nanoda, and cloud costs

A line in the technical note of OpenAI's math repo caught my curiosity: "Compiling the entire library may fail if Linux's vm.max_map_count is too low." I wanted to know what a good value would be and why, and that turned into a larger measurement project: building and checking the whole library (122,458 AI-generated Lean files, about 26 million lines, roughly eleven times Mathlib) on a thermally limited laptop and then on one cloud machine, with a lot of help from Claude Code. The short version: every one of the 416 Comparator configurations is accepted with Lean's kernel at the default limit of 65,530; the only thing that needs more is the aggregate import OAI, which maps about 149,000 files (fails at 148,000, works at 150,000), and most of the mapping budget comes from Mathlib itself, not from the size of OAI. The whole library built in 13.8 hours on a 32-vCPU cloud machine.

I also ran the same checks with the nanoda kernel as a second opinion. It is about five times faster than Lean's replay on a typical config (and scales to 64 threads on the big ones, 672 s against 10.9 hours for the slowest), but the first attempt failed on 15 configurations. I wrote that up, but by the time I posted a bug report, nanoda was already fixed for 14 of them. See issue #55 .

Given what we learned, it might be possible to reproduce a nanoda build with less than $15. The numbers are rough (one laptop, one cloud instance type, uneven load), and I've only minimally reviewed the report, so please treat it as a starting point.

The report, tools and rough data are at openai-math-lean-tooling , starting with REPORT.md. Corrections and reproductions are very welcome, especially about the remaining nanoda failure, and I'd be curious about anyone else's numbers for building OAI on different hardware.

Yes, I know that this is much less about math (where people focus on a small number of results) than infrastructure, but I'm a computer scientist, with a casual interest, and this is what caught my fancy.
One should use con-ron instead of nanoda, right?

In addition to, and also con-leche, if you are paranoid.

With con-leche I processed all but one result, after raising some fuel limits and other perf improvements (now on master). One took too long for me to wait.
